## Who Counts as Unemployed?

The unemployment rate is calculated by dividing the number of unemployed people by the combined number of employed and unemployed people—not by everyone who does not have a job. Whether someone is counted as unemployed depends on specific conditions and the survey’s reference periods.

A person who was not employed during the reference week and was available for work may qualify as unemployed. In most cases, they must also have actively searched for work during the four-week period ending with that reference week. A person on temporary layoff who expects to be recalled may qualify without actively searching. The availability condition has an exception for temporary illness.

By contrast, someone whose only job-search activity was browsing listings has not met the active-search requirement through that activity alone. Unless the temporary-layoff exception applies, they would not qualify as unemployed on that basis. These classifications determine who is included in the unemployed count—and therefore in the unemployment rate’s denominator.
